Then, for any family $f_y \rightarrow f_x$, the Julia set of $f_y$ moves continuously towards the Julia set of $f_x$.
<!-- end lem-13 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Since all indifferent points are persistently indifferent, there is a neighborhood $U_{(x,t)} \in C^n_X$ for all indifferent points $(x,t)$ such that all points of $U_{(x,t)} \cap C^n_X$ are indifferent. Since $\mathrm{pr}_X : C^n_X \rightarrow X$ has finite fibers, it is open by lemma \ref{morphisme fini sur meme dimension est ouvert} and $\mathrm{pr}_X(U_{x,t})$ is open in $X$. Since there are a finite number of indifferent points, we might consider the neighborhood of $x, U := \bigcap U_{x,t}$.

Let $f_y \rightarrow f_x$. 

As in the proof of the theorem \ref{JuliaSetMovesContinuouslyNonArchi}, $J(f_x)$ is contained in the closure of the Julia set of the $f_y$'s. (Each repelling point of $x$ comes from a repelling point, for $y$ close enough to $x$.)

Let now $(y, t_y)$ be some repelling points converging to a point $(x,z)$. For $y$ close enough to $x, y$ belongs to $U$, hence if we look at the connected component containing $(y,t_y)$ it won't give an indifferent point at the intersection with $\mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(x)$ and so it will be a repelling point of $x$. We conclude as in the proof of the theorem \ref{JuliaSetMovesContinuouslyNonArchi}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- ex-8: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean valued field, and let $f$ be a $k$-analytical family of rational map. Let $x \in X$ be such that the classical Julia set of $f$ is non-empty and compact in $\mathbb{P}^{1}(\hat{\overline{k}})$. Then for any family $f_y \rightarrow f_x$, the Julia set of $f_y$ moves continuously towards the Julia set of $f_x$.

We might use proposition \ref{if classical julia set compact, then one attracting only}, to see that $f_x$ has no indifferent points and lemma \ref{If f has no indifferent point, then Julia sets moves continuously} allows us to conclude.
<!-- end ex-8 -->
<!-- nota-1: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean valued field and $K$ be a complete valued field extension. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space without boundary and $f$ a family of rational maps. Let us denote $X_K = X \hat{\otimes} K$ and $f_K$ the family of rational map, $f_K : (X \times_k \mathbb{P}^{1,an}) \hat{\otimes} K \rightarrow (X \times_k \mathbb{P}^{1,an}) \hat{\otimes} K$. Let us denote $\pi^K : (X \times_k \mathbb{P}^{1,an}) \hat{\otimes} K \rightarrow X \times_k \mathbb{P}^{1,an}$ and $\pi^K_X : X_K \rightarrow X$ the two projections.
<!-- end nota-1 -->
<!-- prop-26: body_md -->
\label{If moves continuously on X, then also on X_K}
Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean valued field and $K$ be a complete valued field extension. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space without boundary and $f$ a family of rational maps. 

Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$. Let us assume that there exists $x\in U$ such that $f_x$ has type I repelling points and the Julia set moves continuously on $U$. Then, the Julia set moves continuously on $(\pi^K_X)^{-1}(U)$.
<!-- end prop-26 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Since for any $y \in (\pi^K_X)^{-1}(x),~y$ has type I repelling points and $y \in (\pi^K_X)^{-1}(U)$, it suffices to show that for any $y\in (\pi^K_X)^{-1}(U)$ and $(y,t)$ an indifferent periodic point, then it is persistently indifferent by theorem \ref{JuliaSetMovesContinuouslyNonArchi}. 

Let $y\in (\pi^K_X)^{-1}(U)$ and $(y,t)$ be an indifferent periodic point of some period $l$. By contradiction, let us assume that there exists $(y_n, t_n) \rightarrow (y,t)$ with $t_n$ repelling points of $f_{K,y_n}$ of period dividing $l$.

Then, $\pi^K(y_n, t_n) \rightarrow \pi^K(y,t)$. Let us write $\pi^K(y,t) = (\pi^K_X(y), \tilde{t})$ with $\tilde{t} \in \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathcal{H}(\pi^K_X(y))}$. Hence, $\tilde{t}$ is an indifferent periodic point of $f_{\pi^K_X(y)}$ and $\pi^K_X(y) \in U$. So, it is a persistently indifferent periodic point and $\pi^K(y_n,t_n) = (\pi^K_X(y_n), \tilde{t_n})$ cannot be repelling points and so  $(y_n, t_n)$ cannot be repelling either.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- prop-27: body_md -->
\label{If moves continuously on X_K, then also on X}
Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean valued field and $K$ be a complete valued field extension. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space without boundary and $f$ a family of rational maps. 

Let $U$ be an open subset of $X_K$. Let us assume that there exists $x\in U$ such that $f_x$ has type I repelling points and the Julia set moves continuously on $U$. Then, for any $\emptyset \neq V\subset \pi^K_X(U)$ open, the Julia set moves continuously on $V$.
<!-- end prop-27 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Since the Julia moves continuously on $U$, for any $y\in U, f_y$ has type I repelling points and so does any $y \in (\pi^K_X)(U)$. So, it suffices to show that for any $y\in \pi^K_X(U)$ and $(y,t)$ an indifferent periodic point, then it is persistently indifferent by theorem \ref{JuliaSetMovesContinuouslyNonArchi}. 

Let $y\in \pi^K_X(U)$ and $(y,t)$ be an indifferent periodic point of some period $l$.

By reducing $U$ and keeping only the connected component of an element $\alpha$ of $(\pi^K_X)^{-1}(y)$, we may assume that $U$ is connected and so the type of the periodic point do not change throughout $U$.

Let $\mathcal{V}$ be a neighborhood of $(y,t)$ and let $C^l_\mathcal{V}$ be the analytic space of periodic points of period dividing $l$. By reducing $\mathcal{V}$ me may assume that $C^l_\mathcal{V} \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(y) = \lbrace (y,t)\rbrace$. 

We want to show that for any $(w,z) \in C^l_\mathcal{V}, |(f^l_w)'(z)|=1$.

Let $\mathcal{C} := (\pi^K)^{-1}(C^l_\mathcal{V}) \cap U\times_K\mathbb{P}^{1,an}$. One has $\mathcal{C} \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_{X_K}(\alpha) = \lbrace (w,z), w = \alpha$ and $\pi^K(w,z) = (y,t)\rbrace \cap U\times_K\mathbb{P}^{1,an}$ and all these elements are indifferent periodic points. Since the Julia set moves continuously on $U$, this indifferent point are persistently indifferent, then $\forall (w,z) \in \mathcal{C}, |(f^l_w)'(z)|=1$.

Hence, for any $(w,z) \in C^l_\mathcal{V}, |(f^l_w)'(z)|=1$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- prop-28: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean valued field and $K$ be a complete valued field extension. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space without boundary and $f$ a family of rational maps. 

Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$. Let us assume that there exists $x\in U$ such that $f_x$ has type I repelling points. Then, 
\begin{center}
the Julia set moves continuously on $U \iff$ the Julia set moves continuously on $(\pi^K_X)^{-1}(U)$.
\end{center}
<!-- end prop-28 -->
<!-- prop-29: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a complete, algebraically closed, non-archimedean valued field and $K$ be a complete valued field extension. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space without boundary and $f$ a family of rational maps. Let $\sigma_{K/k}^X : X\rightarrow X_K$ the continuous section from definition \ref{definition universal point and continuous section}. Let $x\in X$ such that $f_x$ has type I repelling points. Then,

\begin{align*}
\mathrm{the~Julia~set~moves~continuously} &\mathrm{~on~a~neighborhood~of~} x\\
&\iff \\
\mathrm{the~Julia~set~moves~continuously} &\mathrm{~on~a~neighborhood~of~} \sigma_{K/k}^X(x).
\end{align*}
<!-- end prop-29 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
$\implies$ This comes from propostion \ref{If moves continuously on X, then also on X_K}.

$\Longleftarrow$ Let $U$ be a neighborhood of $\sigma_{K/k}^X(x)$ such that the Julia set moves continuously.

Then, $V := (\sigma_{K/k}^X)^{-1}(U)$ is a neighborhood of $x$. By contradiction, let us assume that the Julia set does not move continuously on $V$. Then, there exists $y\in V$ and $(y,t)$ an indifferent periodic point of period $l$ and $(y_n, t_n)$ some repelling points with period dividing $l$ and $(y_n, t_n) \rightarrow(y,t)$.

Then, $\sigma_{K/k} (y_n, t_n) \rightarrow \sigma_{K/k}(y,t)$ with $\sigma_{K/k} : X\times \mathbb{P}^{1,an} \rightarrow (X\times \mathbb{P}^{1,an})\hat{\otimes} K$ is the continuous section. Since the Julia set moves continuously on $U$ and $\sigma_{K/k}(y,t) = (\sigma_{K/k}(y), \tilde{t})$ with $\tilde{t} \in \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathcal{H}(\sigma_{K/k}(y))}$ is an indifferent point, the $\sigma_{K/k}(y_n,t_n) = (\sigma_{K/k}(y_n), \tilde{t_n})$ cannot be repelling and so neither $(y_n, t_n)$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- prop-30: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean valued field and $K$ be a complete, valued field extension. And let us assume that the extension $k\subset K$ is algebraic and finite or $K$ is the completion of a normal extension of $K$. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space without boundary and $f$ a family of rational maps. Let $x\in X$ such that $f_x$ has type I repelling points. Then the following are equivalent :

\begin{enumerate}
\item The Julia set moves continuously on a neighborhood of $x$,
\item The Julia set moves continuously on a neighborhood of all $y  \in (\pi_{K/k}^X)^{-1}(x)$,
\item The Julia set moves continuously on a neighborhood of one $y  \in (\pi_{K/k}^X)^{-1}(x)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-30 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
$1 \implies 2$ is proposition \ref{If moves continuously on X, then also on X_K}.

$2\implies 3$ is clear.

$3\implies 1$ Let $y  \in (\pi_{K/k}^X)^{-1}(x)$ such that the Julia set moves continously on one of its neighborhood $U$.

One needs to show that $\pi^K_X$ is open. If the field extension is finite, it is clear. If it is the completion of a normal extension, then it comes from Proposition 1.3.5 and Corollary 1.3.6 of \cite{BerkovichLivre} which states that for any such $K$, and any Banach algebra $A$ over $k$, then :
\begin{center}
$\mathcal{M}(A\hat{\otimes}K) /\mathrm{Gal}(k^{sep}/k) \rightarrow \mathcal{M}(A)$
\end{center}
is a homeomorphism where $k^{sep}$ is the separable closure of $k$ in $K$. The oppeness of the quotient map $\mathcal{M}(A\hat{\otimes}K) \rightarrow \mathcal{M}(A\hat{\otimes}K) /\mathrm{Gal}(k^{sep}/k)$ shows the openness of $\pi^K_X$.

Since $\pi^K_X$ is open, $\pi^K_X(U)$ is a neighborhood of $x$ and by proposition \ref{If moves continuously on X_K, then also on X}, the Julia set moves continuously on it.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- prop-31: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a complete, non-archimedean valued field and $K$ be a complete valued field extension. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space without boundary and $f$ a family of rational maps. Let $x\in X$ such that $f_x$ has type I repelling point. Assume that $\mathrm{Int}((\pi^K_X)^{-1}(x)) \neq \emptyset$. Then, the Julia set moves continuously on $\mathrm{Int}((\pi^K_X)^{-1}(x))$.
<!-- end prop-31 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Let $y \in \mathrm{Int}((\pi^K_X)^{-1}(x))$ and let $(y,t)$ be an indifferent point of period $l$, we need to show that it is persistently indifferent.

If not, then there exists $y_n \in \mathrm{Int}((\pi^K_X)^{-1}(x))$ and $(y_n,t_n)$ repelling points of $f_{y_n}$ with period dividing $l$ and $(y_n, t_n) \rightarrow (y,t)$.

Then, $\pi^K(y_n, t_n) \rightarrow \pi^K(y,t)$ and $\pi^K(y_n, t_n) = (x, \tilde{t_n}), \pi^K(y,t) = (x, \tilde{t})$ with $\tilde{t_n}, \tilde{t} \in \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathcal{H}(x)}$. But $(x, \tilde{t_n}) \in J_x$ since they are repelling periodic points of $f_x$ and $(x, \tilde{t}) \notin J_x$ since it is an indifferent periodic point of $f_x$, which is a contradiction to the fact that $J_x$ is closed.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- defi-24: body_md -->
\label{definition of continuous motion in M_d^an}
Let $k$ be a complete valued field and let $\mathrm{M}_d^{an}$ be the analytification of $\mathrm{M}_d$ and let $\pi^{an} : \mathrm{Rat}_d^{an} \rightarrow \mathrm{M}_d^{an}$ the analytification of the projection morphism. Let $U$ be an open subset of $\mathrm{M}_d^{an}$, then we say that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$ if the following condition is verified:
\begin{center}
$\forall [f] \in \mathcal{U}, \forall \tilde{f} \in (\pi^{an})^{-1}([f])$ there exists $\tilde{f} \in U_{\tilde{f}} \subset \mathrm{Rat}_d^{an}$ such that the Julia set moves continuously on $U_{\tilde{f}}$.
\end{center}
<!-- end defi-24 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{Theorem of Marco Maculan}(Theorem 1.6, \cite{MaculanGIT})

Let $k$ be a complete valued field, $X$ a $k$-affine scheme and $G$ a reductive, algebraic group acting on $X$. Then the morphism $\pi^{an} : X^{an} \rightarrow (X//G)^{an}$ satisfies the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\pi^{an}$ is surjective and $G^{an}$-invariant,
\item for every $x, x' \in X^{an}$,
\begin{center}
$\pi^{an}(x) = \pi^{an}(x')$ if and only if $\overline{G^{an}\cdot x} \cap \overline{G^{an}\cdot x'} \neq \emptyset$,
\end{center}
\item for every $U \subset X^{an}$ open, $G^{an}$-stable, the projection $\pi^{an}(U)$ is open. 
\end{itemize}
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- prop-32: body_md -->
\label{Construction of SL2 invariant open}
Let $k$ be a complete valued field and $X$ be an affine $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant subscheme of $\mathrm{Rat}_d$. Let $f \in X^{an}$ such that there exists $f\in U$ such that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$ and all $g$ in $U$ have type I repelling points. 

Let us define 
\begin{center}
$W = \lbrace x \in X^{an}, \exists M \in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}, M\cdot x \in U \rbrace.$
\end{center}
Then, $W$ is an open, $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant and the Julia set moves continuously on $W$.
<!-- end prop-32 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
First, $W$ is clearly $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant. 

Let us show that for $x \in W$, we may find $M \in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}(\widehat{\overline{\mathcal{H}(x)}})$ such that $M\cdot x \in U$.  

Let us denote $\Omega : \mathrm{SL}_2^{an}\times X^{an} \rightarrow X^{an}$ the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2^{an}$. Let $x \in W$. There exists $h\in\mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}$ such that $(h,x) \in \Omega^{-1}(U)$ and $\Omega^{-1}(U) \cap \mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(x)$ is an open of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}$. Since $x$ has repelling type I points, $\mathcal{H}(x)$ is not trivially valued and so the rigid points are dense in $\mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}$. Hence, there exists $M \in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}(\widehat{\overline{\mathcal{H}(x)}}) \cap (\Omega^{-1}(U) \cap \mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(x)).$

If $W$ is not open, then there exists $x\in W$ and $x_n \notin W \rightarrow x$ since the Berkovich spaces are angelic (see \cite{PoineauAngelique}).
Let $M\in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}(\widehat{\overline{\mathcal{H}(x)}})$ such that $M\cdot x\in U$. 

By proposition 3.27 of \cite{RoyActionGroupe}, there exists $M_n \in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x_n)}^{an}$ such that $(M_n, x_n) \rightarrow (M,x) \in (\mathrm{SL}_2\times X)^{an}$. Hence, $\Omega(M_n, x_n) \rightarrow \Omega(M,x) \in U$. So, for $n$ big enough $\Omega(M_n, x_n) \in U$ and $x_n \in W$.

Hence, $W$ is a $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant open subset of $X^{an}$. It remains to show that the Julia set moves continuously on $W$. So we need to show that for all $g \in W$ any indifferent fixed point is persistently indifferent. 

Let $g \in W$, and $t$ an indifferent point of $g$. Since $g \in W$, there exists $M \in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}(\widehat{\overline{\mathcal{H}(x)}})$ such that $g^M \in U$. Then, $M^{-1}\cdot t$ is an indifferent point of $g^M$. 

Let us assume that $(g_n, t_n) \rightarrow (g,t)$ with $t_n$ a periodic point of $g_n$ of the same period as $t$. Then, by proposition 3.27 of \cite{RoyActionGroupe}, there exists $M_n \in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x_n)}^{an}$ such that $(M_n, g_n, t_n) \rightarrow (M, g, t) \in (\mathrm{SL}_2\times X \times \mathbb{P}^1_k)^{an}$. Then $(g_n^{M_n}, M_n^{-1} \cdot t_n) \rightarrow (g^M, M^{-1}\cdot t)$ and $M_n^{-1} \cdot t_n$ is a periodic point of $g_n^{M_n}$ of same period of $M^{-1}\cdot t$. Since $M^{-1}\cdot t$ is persistently indifferent, for $n$ big enough, $M_n^{-1}\cdot t_n$ is indifferent, hence so is $t_n$ and finally $t$ is persistently indifferent.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- prop-33: body_md -->
\label{Julia moves continuously on Rat_d is the same as in M_d}
Let $k$ be a complete valued field and $X$ be an affine $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant subscheme of $\mathrm{Rat}_d$. Let $f \in X^{an}$ such that $f$ has repelling type I points and let $\pi^{an} : X^{an} \subset \mathrm{Rat}_d^{an}\rightarrow (X/\mathrm{SL}_2)^{an}\subset \mathrm{M}_d^{an}$. Then,
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{There~is~a~neighborhood~of~}f \in &X^{an} \mathrm{~such~that~the~Julia~set~moves~continuously}\\
&\iff\\ 
\mathrm{There~is~a~neighborhood~of~}\pi^{an}(f) \in& (X/\mathrm{SL}_2)^{an} \mathrm{~such~that~the~Julia~set~moves~continuously.} 
\end{align*}
<!-- end prop-33 -->
<!-- rem-11: body_md -->
Here we only consider familes of rational maps that are defined by algebraic families because it is the setting where the construction of the $M_n$ are defined in \cite{RoyActionGroupe}. Nevertheless smoooth analytic spaces are locally algebraic (see for example, 0.21 of \cite{DucrosModelTheory} which relies on Theorem 3.4.1 of \cite{BerkovichEtaleCohomology}) and so, the result will stand if we have a smooth analytic family of rational maps.
<!-- end rem-11 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
$\Longleftarrow$ It is clear by definition.

$\Longrightarrow$ Let $f\in U \subset X^{an}$ such that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$. Then, we can define $W$ as in proposition \ref{Construction of SL2 invariant open} and by theorem \ref{Theorem of Marco Maculan} (of Maculan \cite{MaculanGIT}), $\pi^{an}(W)$ is open and contains $\pi^{an}(f)$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- defi-25: body_md -->
Let $X$ a $\mathbb{C}_{hyb}$-analytic space. An analytic family of rational maps of degree $d\geq 2$, parametrized by $X$, is an analytic map $f : X \times_{\mathbb{C}_{hyb}} \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathbb{C}_{hyb}} \rightarrow X\times_{\mathbb{C}_{hyb}} \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathbb{C}_{hyb}}$ such that $\mathrm{pr}_X = \mathrm{pr}_X \circ f$ where $\mathrm{pr}_X : X\times_{\mathbb{C}_{hyb}} \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathbb{C}_{hyb}}$ is the projection and for all $x \in X, f_x := f(x, \cdot) : \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathcal{H}(x)} \rightarrow \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathcal{H}(x)}$ is a rational map of degree $d\geq 2$.
<!-- end defi-25 -->
<!-- prop-34: body_md -->
\label{if no indifferent point, then julia set moves continuously in the hybrid setting}
Let $f \in (\mathrm{Rat}_d)_0$ be a rational function. Let assume that $f$ has no indifferent points. Then the Julia set moves continuously at $f$, in the sense that if $f_i \rightarrow f$, then 
\begin{center}
$\mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, z_i), z_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}(f) = \lbrace (f,x), x\in J_f\rbrace$ 
\end{center}
with $\mathrm{pr} : \mathrm{Rat}_d\times \mathbb{P}^{1,an} \rightarrow \mathbb{P}^{1,an}$.
<!-- end prop-34 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
By theorem \ref{NumberAttractingPointsBounded}, we see that $f$ has type I repelling points and by proposition \ref{2 attracting points implies infinitely many}, we see that $f$ has exactly one non-repelling point, which is attracting. Furthermore, by proposition \ref{repelling points of type I are dense in the Julia Set}, the type I repelling points are dense in the Julia set. 

By lemma \ref{If f has no indifferent point, then Julia sets moves continuously}, one sees that if we have a family $f_i \in (\mathrm{Rat}_d)_0 \rightarrow f$ then, the Julia set of $f_i$ moves continuously towards the Julia set of $f$.

Let $f_i \in (\mathrm{Rat}_d)_{>0} \rightarrow f$. 

Let $z$ be a repelling point of $f$ and let $V$ be a neighborhood of $(f,z)$ small and $C^n_V$, the closed analytic space defined in the same way as in definition \ref{Definition of the periodic point}. By reducing $V$ we might consider that in the entire connected component of $C^n_V$ that contains $(f,z)$ the points are repelling. Hence, for all $i$ big enough, we may consider $z_i$ a repelling point of $f_i$ such that $(f_i, z_i) \rightarrow (f,z)$.

Hence, we have $\lbrace (f,x), x\in J_f\rbrace \subset \mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, z_i), z_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}(f)$.

Let us now consider $(f_i, z_i)$ with $z_i$ a repelling point of $f_i$. We can assume that $(f_i, z_i)$ converges to some $(f,x)$. We need to show that $x \in J_f$. For each $z_i$ let us denote $n_i$ the period of the cycle and we might look at $C^{n_i}_{U\times \mathbf{A}^{1,an}}$ where $U$ is a neighborhood of $f$ that contains $f_i$ for $i$ big enough. Then, for each $z_i$ we might look at the connected component where $(f_i, z_i)$ belongs. It crosses $\mathrm{pr}^{-1}(f)$ at some point $(f, z_i^f)$ which is necessarily repelling since all the periodic points of $f$ are repelling.

Then $(f,x)$ is a cluster point of the $(f, z_i^f)$. If not we may find $V, V'$ two open subsets such that $(f,x) \in V, (f, z_i^f)\in V'$ and $V \cap V' = \emptyset$, but for $i$ big enough, it would imply that $(f_i, z_i) \in V'$ which is a contradiction to the fact that $(f_i, z_i) \rightarrow (f,x)$. 

Hence, we have $\mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, z_i), z_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}(f) \subset \lbrace (f,x), x\in J_f\rbrace$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- rem-12: body_md -->
\label{If infinitely many non repelling then no continuous motion}
The condition of the previous proposition implies that there are a finite number of non-repellings points which is a necessary condition to have continuity of the Julia set.

Indeed, since the number of non-repelling points of $f\in \mathrm{Rat}_d(\mathbb{C})$ is bounded by $2d-2$, there can be at most $2d-2$ non-repelling periodic point for $f\in Rat_{d,0}$. Hence, if the Julia set moves continuously at $f\in \mathrm{Rat}_{d,0}$, either $f$ has one attracting point and all the others are repelling or there is $\leq 2d-2$ indifferent point and no attractiong point. This comes from propositionn \ref{2 attracting points implies infinitely many} which states that if they are an attracting point and an other non repelling point, then they are infinitely many non repelling points in the non-archimedean case.
<!-- end rem-12 -->
<!-- ex-9: body_md -->
Let $f(z) = z^2 + c \in (\mathrm{Rat}_2)_0$ with $|c| > 1$. Then the Julia set moves continuously at $f$.
<!-- end ex-9 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
As seen in lemma \ref{z^2+ T has only repelling points}, $f$ has no indifferent point. Therefore, we can use proposition \ref{if no indifferent point, then julia set moves continuously in the hybrid setting} to conclude.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lem-14: body_md -->
\label{JuliaSetSemiContinuous}
Let $k$ be a valued field. Let $X$ be a $k$-analytic space (in this case, $k$ is suppose to be complete) or a $k_{hyb}$-flowing, analytic space. Let $f : X\times \mathbb{P}^1 \rightarrow X\times \mathbb{P}^1$ an analytic family of rational maps of degree $d$. 

Let $f_{x_i} \in X \rightarrow f_x\in X$, then 
\begin{center}
$\lbrace (f_x, z), z\in J(f_x)\rbrace \subset \mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_{x_i}, z), z \in J(f_{x_i})\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}_X^{-1}(f_x)$.
\end{center}
<!-- end lem-14 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
This is a direct consequence of Poineau's theorem (see Théorème 6.26 \cite{PoineauDynamique}). This theorem states that the family of equilibrium measure associated to each $f_y$ is continuous and since the Julia set of $f_y$ is the support of the equilibrium measure of $f_y$, the lower semicontinuity follows.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- defi-26: body_md -->
\label{def filled julia set, escape radius}
Let $k$ be a complete valued field and $f$ be a polynomial of degree $d \geq 2$ defined over $k$. Then one defines the filled Julia set as a closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^{1,an}_k$ in the following manner :
\begin{center}
$K_f := \lbrace x \in \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_k, f^{\circ n}(x) \nrightarrow \infty \rbrace.$
\end{center}

We can see $\mathcal{P}_d$, the set of polynomials of degree $d$ as a closed subscheme of $\mathrm{Rat}_d$.

For each $f \in \mathcal{P}_d$, one can define the escape radius 
\begin{center}
$R_f := \frac{1 + |a_d| + \cdots +|a_0|}{|a_d|} = \eta_f(\frac{b_0^{2d}}{\rho})^{\frac{1}{d}} + \eta_f(\frac{a_d^d b_0^d}{\rho})^{\frac{1}{d}}+ \cdots + \eta_f(\frac{a_0^d b_0^d}{\rho})^{\frac{1}{d}}$.
\end{center}
It defines a continuous function $\mathcal{P}_d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_+$. Furthermore, $K_f = \lbrace x \in \mathbb{P}^{1,an}, \forall n ~ |T(f^{\circ n}(x))|\leq R_f\rbrace$, where we see $f^{\circ n}(x)$ as an element of $\mathbb{P}^{1,an}$.
<!-- end defi-26 -->
<!-- prop-35: body_md -->
(Theorem 8.15, (f), of \cite{BenedettoLivre})

Let $k$ be a complete valued field and $f$ be a polynomial of degree $d \geq 2$ defined over $k$. Then, 
\begin{center}
$J_f = \delta K_f$.
\end{center}
<!-- end prop-35 -->
<!-- prop-36: body_md -->
Let $k$ be a complete valued field or a hybrid field, then the filled Julia set is upper semicontinuous on $P^{an}_d$.
<!-- end prop-36 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Let $f \in \mathcal{P}_d^{an}$ and let $f_i \rightarrow f$. Let $z\in \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathcal{H}(f)}$ such that there exists $z_i \in K_{x_i}$ and $(f_i, z_i) \rightarrow (f,z)$. Let $U$ be a neighborhood of $(f,z)$ such that the coefficients $a_i, b_i$ of $f$ are elements of $\mathcal{O}(U)$, then $F^{\circ n} : (f,z) \mapsto f^{\circ n}(z) \in \mathcal{H}(f,z)$ is an element of $\mathcal{O}(U)$ and for $i$ big enough, $(f_i, z_i) \in U$. 

Then, $|F^{\circ n}(f_i, z_i)| \rightarrow |F^{\circ n}(f, z)|$ and $|F^{\circ n}(f_i, z_i)|\leq R_{f_i}$. Since $R_{f_i} \rightarrow R_f$, one gets $z \in K_f$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
Let $f \in (\mathcal{P}_d)_0$ be a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ such that $K_f$ has empty interior, then the Julia set moves continuously at $f$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- rem-13: body_md -->
The case where $K_f$ has empty interior is the case where $f$ has only one non-repelling point which is attracting. Furthermore, in this case the classical Julia set is non-empty and compact, by Trucco \cite{TruccoWanderingFatouComp} if $K$ is the algebraic closure of a discretely valued field.  

In fact, Trucco showed that if $f \in (P_d^{an})_0$, then the Julia set is the disjoint union of the grand orbit of a finite number of repelling type II points and the classical Julia set (Theorem A, \cite{TruccoWanderingFatouComp}). If there is a type II repelling point, then there are infinitely many non-repelling points, hence there cannot be a continuous motion of the Julia sets, see remark \ref{If infinitely many non repelling then no continuous motion}.

Furthermore, he proved that in the polynomial case, the fact that the classical Julia set is non-empty and compact is equivalent to the fact that all the non-infinity periodic points are repelling (Corollary 7.15, \cite{TruccoWanderingFatouComp}). Hence, this implies the following result.
<!-- end rem-13 -->
<!-- prop-37: body_md -->
Let $f \in (\mathcal{P}_d)_0$ be a polynomial of degree $d \geq 2$. Then, the Julia sets moves continuously at $f$ if and only if $f$ has only repelling points and $\infty$ as an attracting point. 
Furthermore if $\mathcal{H}(f)$ is discretely valued, then it is also equivalent to the classical Julia set of $f$ being compact in $\mathbb{P}^1(\hat{\overline{\mathcal{H}(f)}})$.
<!-- end prop-37 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
The second if and only if comes directly from the corollary 7.15 of Trucco, \cite{TruccoWanderingFatouComp}, and lemma \ref{compact of k are compact in berkovich}. 

The first implication comes from theorem A of Trucco, \cite{TruccoWanderingFatouComp}, since it shows that the classical Julia set is not compact if and only if $f$ has a type II repelling point which implies that it has infinitely many non-repelling points.

The converse implication is proposition \ref{if no indifferent point, then julia set moves continuously in the hybrid setting}.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- ex-10: body_md -->
\label{continuity in hybrid is not continuity on U_0 and U_>0}
Let $t \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|t|<1$. Let $f_t(z) = tz^3 + z^2$, then the critical point of $f_t$ are $z_t = 0$ and $z_t = -\frac{2}{3t}$, hence for $|t|<1$ the critical points are never in the Julia set. So the Julia moves continuously, in the archimedean case, by the caracterisation of the continuity of the Julia set with the crititcal points (see for example Theorem 4.2, 7. of \cite{McMullenComplexDynamicsAndRenormalization}). 

We saw in lemma \ref{Tz^3 + Z^2 moves continuously} that the Julia set moves continuously on $D^{an}(0,1)_{(\mathbb{C}, |\cdot|_0)}$. But if we take $f_T \in (Rat_d)_0$ it has infinitely many non-repelling points, so the Julia set cannot move continuously in the hybrid case since in the archimedean case, there is only finitely many non-repelling points.
<!-- end ex-10 -->
<!-- lem-15: body_md -->
\label{Julia set is invariant through the flow}
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ a flowing $\mathbb{C}_{hyb}$-analytic space. Let $f$ be an analytic family of rational maps. Then, the Julia set is inviariant through the flow.

In the sense that if $(x,z) \in J_x$ with $J_x$ embedded in $X\times \mathbb{P}^{1,hyb}$, then for any $\alpha \in (0, \frac{1}{\mathrm{pr} (x,z)}, (x,z)^\alpha \in J_{x^\alpha}$.
<!-- end lem-15 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Let $(x,z) \in J_x$. Since the repelling points are dense in $J_x$ (proposition \ref{Repelling points are dense}), it is enough to show that $(x,z)^\alpha \in J_{x^\alpha}$ with $z$ a repelling point.

If $z$ is a type I repelling point, then $z^{\alpha}$ is also a type I repelling point of $x^\alpha$ since $|f'_{x^\alpha}(z^\alpha)| = |f'_x(z)|^\alpha$ and $(x,z)^\alpha \in J_{x^\alpha}$.

If $z$ is a type II repelling point, then there exists $M \in \mathrm{SL}_2(\overline{\mathcal{H}(x)})$ such that $M\cdot z = \eta_{0,1}$ and $f_x^M$ has a reduction in $\tilde{\mathcal{H}(x)}$ of degree at least 2.

Since, $M^\alpha \cdot z^\alpha = (M\cdot z)^\alpha$ and $(f_x^\alpha)^{M^\alpha} = (f_x^M)^\alpha$ and the reduction of $f^M_x$ and $(f_x^\alpha)^{M^\alpha}$ have same degree, $z^\alpha$ is a type II repelling point of $f_x^\alpha$ and $(x,z)^\alpha \in J_{x^\alpha}$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lem-16: body_md -->
\label{Julia set moves continously on neighborhood is the same as on a flowing neighborhood}
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ a flowing $\mathbb{C}_{hyb}$-analytic space. Let $f$ be an analytic family of rational maps. Let $x\in X$ and $U$ a neighborhood of $x$ such that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$. 

Then, the Julia set moves continuously on $T(U)$, the trajectory of $U$ which is an open flowing neighborhood.
<!-- end lem-16 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Let $y \in T(U)$ and $y_i \rightarrow y$. Since $y \in T(U)$, there exists $\alpha \in (0, \frac{1}{\mathrm{pr} (y)}]$ such that $y^\alpha \in U$. 

If $\mathrm{pr}(y) \neq 0$ and $\alpha = \frac{1}{\mathrm{pr} (y)}$, then we define $\alpha_i = \frac{1}{\mathrm{pr} (y_i)}$. If not then for $i$ big enough, $\alpha < \frac{1}{\mathrm{pr} (y_i)}$ and we define $\alpha_i = \alpha$.

Either way, we have $y_i^{\alpha_i} \rightarrow y^\alpha \in U$.

Let $z_i \in J_{y_i}$ and let $(y,z)$ a cluster point of $(y_i, z_i)$. We want to show that $z \in J_y$. Let us assume that $(y_i, z_i) \rightarrow (y,z)$. 

Since $(y_i, z_i)^{\alpha_i} \rightarrow (y,z)^\alpha$ and the Julia set moves continuously on $U, (y,z)^\alpha$ is a point of the embedding of $J_{y^\alpha}$ in $X\times\mathbb{P}^{1,hyb}$. So, $z\in J_y$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lem-17: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ a flowing $\mathbb{C}_{hyb}$-analytic space. Let $f$ be an analytic family of rational maps. Then, the closed analytic space of periodic point of period $n, C^n_X$ is flowing.
<!-- end lem-17 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
It is clear by definition of $C^n_X$.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- defi-27: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ a flowing $\mathbb{C}_{hyb}$-analytic space. Let $f$ be an analytic family of rational maps and $x \in X_0$. A periodic point $z \in \mathbb{P}^{1,an}_{\mathcal{H}(x)}$ of $f_x$ of period $n$ of type I is said to be hybridly persistently non reppelling if it is persistently indifferent on $X_0$ and there is a flowing neighborhood $U$ of $(x,z)$ such that if $V$ be the connected component of $C^n_U$ containing $(x,z)$ and $V^1, \cdots, V^m$ are the connected components of $V_{>0}$, then for all $i$ we are in one of the following cases : 
\begin{itemize}
    \item for all $(y,t) \in V^i,~t$ is an attracting point of $f_y$, 
    \item for all $(y,t) \in V^i,~t$ is an indifferent point of $f_y$ not in the Julia set $J_{f_y}$. 
\end{itemize}
<!-- end defi-27 -->
<!-- rem-14: body_md -->
This definition is really a local definition : if $U$ is the neighborhood in the definition, then any other flowing neighborhood $U'\subset U$ will satisfy the conditions of the definition.
<!-- end rem-14 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{Julia set moves continuously hybrid setting}
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ a flowing $\mathbb{C}_{hyb}$-analytic space. Let $f$ be an analytic family of rational maps and $x \in X$ such that $x$ has type I repelling points. 

\begin{itemize}
\item If $x \in X_{>0}$, then the Julia set moves continuously on a neighborhood of $x$ if and only if it moves continuously on a neighborhood $U$ of $x$ in the fiber $X_{\mathrm{pr}(x)}$,

\item If $x\in X_0$, then the Julia set moves continuously on a neighborhood of $x$ if and only if there is a flowing neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that :
\begin{enumerate}
\item the Julia sets moves continuously on $U_{>0}$,
\item for all $y\in U_0$, every indifferent point of $f_y$ is hybridly persistently non-repelling.
\end{enumerate} 
\end{itemize}
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- rem-15: body_md -->
In the non-archimedean case, one has to assume that $X$ does not have a boundary, but it is not needed here. The reason is that the definition differs on the case of Berkovich spaces over a complete field and in the general case. In the general case one only considers spaces without boundary.

For instance, the closed ball center on $0$ of radius $1$ in $\mathbf{A}^{1,an}_k$ is an analytic space but the closed ball center on $0$ of radius $1$ in $\mathbf{A}^{1,hyb}_\mathbb{C}$ is not.
<!-- end rem-15 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
By lemma \ref{Julia set moves continously on neighborhood is the same as on a flowing neighborhood}, we can work with flowing neighborhood.

First let us assume that $x\in X_{> 0}$. If $U$ is a flowing neighborhood of $x$, then so is $U_{>0}$. Hence, we may assume that $U$ is of the form $U_{>0}$.

$\implies$ If the Julia set moves continuously on $U$ then it moves continuously on $U_{\mathrm{pr}(x)} = U \cap X_{\mathrm{pr}(x)}$.

$\Longleftarrow$ Let us assume that the Julia set moves continuously on a neighborhood $U_{\mathrm{pr}(x)}$ of $x$ in $X_{\mathrm{pr}(x)})$. Then, $U := T(U_{\mathrm{pr}(x)})$ is a flowing open subset. 

Let $f\in U$ and let $f_i \in U \rightarrow f$. Let us denote $\varepsilon = \mathrm{pr}(f), \varepsilon_i = \mathrm{pr}(f_i)$. 

One needs to check that 
\begin{center}
$\mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, z_i), z_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(f) = \lbrace (f, z), z\in J_f\rbrace$. 
\end{center}

Since the repelling points remain repelling locally, one has $\lbrace (f, z), z\in J_f\rbrace \subset \mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, z_i), z_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(f)$.

Let $(f_i, z_i) \rightarrow (f,z)$ with $z_i \in J_{f_i}$. One needs to check that $z \in J_f$. We have that $(f_i, z_i)^{\frac{\mathrm{pr}(x)}{\varepsilon_i}} \rightarrow (f,z)^{\frac{\mathrm{pr}(x)}{\varepsilon}}$ and since the Julia set moves continuously on $U_{\mathrm{pr}(x)}$, one has $z^{\frac{\mathrm{pr}(x)}{\varepsilon}} \in J_{f^{\frac{\mathrm{pr}(x)}{\varepsilon}}}$. Hence, $z\in J_f$ by lemma \ref{Julia set is invariant through the flow}.

Now let us assume that $x\in X_0$. 

$\implies$ Let us assume that the Julia set moves continuously on a flowing neighborhood $U$ of $x$. Then it moves continuously on the open $U_{>0}$ and the open $U_0$ of $X_0$. 

Let $y \in U_0$. Since the Julia set moves continuously on $U_0$, all indifferent point of $y$ are persistently indifferent on $U_0$. Let $(y,t)$ be an indifferent point of $y$ of period $n$. Let $V$ be a flowing neighborhood of $(y,t)$ and let $C = C^n_V$. It is a flowing analytic space. Let $V^i$ be a connected component of $C_{>0}$ and $0 < \varepsilon \leq 1$, then $V_\varepsilon^i$ is a connected component of $C_\varepsilon$. Since $t \notin J_y$ we may suppose that for all $(f,z) \in V^i, z\notin J_f$. So for all, $(f,z) \in V^i_\varepsilon, |(f^n)'(z)|\leq 1$. We have two separate cases, either it atteins 1 or not. If it atteins 1, by the maximum modulus principle, it is contant to the value 1 on all $V^i_\varepsilon$, otherwise it is always $<1$. Since $V^i$ is flowing, this behavior remains true in all $V^i$ : either for all points $(f,z) \in V^i, |(f^n)'(z)| <1$ or for all points $(f,z) \in V^i, |(f^n)'(z)| = 1$. And $(y,t)$ is hybridly persistently non-repelling. 

$\Longleftarrow$ Let us assume that there exists a flowing neighborhood $U$ of $x$ such that the Julia set moves continuously on $U_{>0}$ and for all $y\in U_0$, every indifferent point of $y$ is hybridly persistently non-repelling. 

Let us show that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$. 
Let $f\in U$. If $f\in U_{>0}$ since the Julia set moves continuously on $U_{>0}$, we have that for all $f_i \rightarrow f,$ the $\mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, z_i), z_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(f) = \lbrace (f, z), z\in J_f\rbrace$.     

Let us now assume that $f\in U_0$. Let $f_i \rightarrow f$. Let $(f_i, z_i) \rightarrow (f,z)$ with $z_i$ repelling point. One needs to show that $z\in J_f$. Let us look at the two subnets $\lbrace f_i, f_i \in U_0\rbrace, \lbrace f_i, f_i \in U_{>0}\rbrace$. Since at least one of them has an infinite number of elements, we may suppose that the net is of one of this form to show that $z$ has to be in $J_f$.  

Since all its indifferent points are persistently indifferent in $U_0$, if $f_i \in U_0 \rightarrow f$, the Julia set of $f_i$ moves continuously to $J_f$ by theorem \ref{JuliaSetMovesContinuouslyNonArchi} and $z\in J_f$. 

So, let $f_i \in U_{>0} \rightarrow f$. As in the previous case, one needs to show :  
\begin{center}
$\mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, t_i), t_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(f) = \lbrace (f, t), t\in J_f\rbrace$. 
\end{center}

Since the repelling points remain repelling locally, one has $\lbrace (f, t), t\in J_f\rbrace \subset \mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, t_i), t_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(f)$.

Each $z_i$ is in a connected component $V^i$ of some $(C^{n_{z_i}}_V)_{>0}$ where $V$ is a flowing open subset containing $(f_i, z_i)$ such that $\mathrm{pr}_X(V) = U$. Let $z^f_i$ be a point of $(C^{n_{z_i}}_V) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(f)$ such that it is a cluster point of $V^i$. Since $z_i$ is repelling, $z^f_i$ cannot be indifferent, since the indifferent point of $f$ are persistently hybridly non-repelling. Hence, they are repelling. 

As in the proof of theorem \ref{JuliaSetMovesContinuouslyNonArchi}, $(f,z)$ is a cluster point of $(f_i, z^f_i)$. 

So, $z\in J_f$ and  $\mathrm{Closure}(\lbrace (f_i, z_i), z_i \in J_{f_i}\rbrace) \cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}_X(f) \subset \lbrace (f, z), z\in J_f\rbrace$.

Finally, we conclude that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- rem-16: body_md -->
We have here a difference with the archimedean and non-archimedean case : an indifferent periodic point of a point $f_x \in X_0$ can come from an attracting point of some $f_{x_i} \in X_{>0} \rightarrow f_x$. This cannot happen in the other cases : the type of the attracting point never changes throughout a neighborhood.

But we do not have an example where such a case occurs.
<!-- end rem-16 -->
<!-- defi-28: body_md -->
\label{definition of continuous motion in M_d^hyb}
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and let $\mathrm{M}_d^{hyb}$ be the analytification of $\mathrm{M}_d$. Let $U$ be a open, flowing subset of $\mathrm{M}_d^{hyb}$. We say that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$ if the following condition is verified:
\begin{center}
$\forall [f] \in U, \forall \tilde{f} \in (\pi^{hyb})^{-1}([f])$ there exists a neighborhood $U_{\tilde{f}}$ of $\tilde{f}$ in $\mathrm{Rat}_d^{hyb}$ such that the Julia set moves continuously on $U_{\tilde{f}}$, 
\end{center}
where $\pi^{hyb} : \mathrm{Rat}_d^{hyb} \rightarrow \mathrm{M}_d^{hyb}$ is the analytification of the projection morphism.
<!-- end defi-28 -->
<!-- prop-38: body_md -->
\label{Construction of SL2 invariant open in hybrid setting}

Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ be an affine $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant subscheme of $\mathrm{Rat}_d$. Let $f \in X^{hyb}$. Assume that there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $f$ such that the Julia set moves continuously on $U$ and $U$ is flowing. 

Let us define 
\begin{center}
$W = \lbrace x \in X^{hyb}, \exists M \in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}, M\cdot x \in U \rbrace.$
\end{center}
Then, $W$ is an open, $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant, flowing and the Julia set moves continuously on $W$.
<!-- end prop-38 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
First let us assume that $f\in X_{>0}$. Then, we may assume that $U \subset X_{>0}$. Then, for all $M\in \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C}), M\cdot U$ is an open that contains $M\cdot f$ and the Julia set moves continuously on this open. Furthermore, $W = \bigcup_{M\in \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})} M\cdot U$, hence it is open, $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant and the Julia set moves continuously on $W$.

If $f \in X_0$, the proof that $W$ is open and that the Julia set moves continuously on $W$ is the same as in the proof of proposition \ref{Construction of SL2 invariant open}. The only thing we need to check is that if $x\in W_0$ then $\mathcal{H}(x)$ is not trivially valued and one needs to consider generalised sequences and not sequences as we do not know if the hybrid spaces are angelic. 

Let $x \in W_0$ and let $M\in \mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}$ such that $M\cdot x \in U$. Hence, $M\cdot x$ does not have potential good reduction : it has repelling type I points since the Julia moves continuously on $U$. Since $M$ is not necessarily a rigid point of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,\mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}$, one needs propositon 4.14 of \cite{RoyActionGroupe} to conclude that $x$ does not have potential good reduction either and so $\mathcal{H}(x)$ cannot be trivially valued. 

We are left to show that $W$ is flowing. Let $x \in W$ and $\alpha \in (0, \frac{1}{\mathrm{pr}(x)}]$, where $\mathrm{pr} : X^{hyb} \rightarrow \mathcal{M}(\mathbb{C}_{hyb})$. Let $M \in \mathrm{SL}_{2, \mathcal{H}(x)}^{an}(\widehat{\overline{\mathcal{H}(x)}})$ such that $M\cdot x \in U$. Then, $(M\cdot x)^\alpha = M^\alpha \cdot x^\alpha$ and $M^\alpha \in \mathrm{SL}_{2, \mathcal{H}(x^\alpha)}^{an}(\widehat{\overline{\mathcal{H}(x^\alpha)}})$. 

Since, $U$ is flowing, $(M\cdot x)^\alpha \in U$ and so $x^\alpha \in W$ and $W$ is flowing.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- prop-39: body_md -->
\label{pi^hyb is open under some conditions} (Proposition 4.25 of \cite{RoyActionGroupe})

Let $X$ be an affine scheme over a non-trivially valued field $k,~ G$ be a reductive, algebraic group acting on $X$ with a closed action. 

Let $V \subset X^{hyb}$ be a flowing, $G$-invariant open subset of $X^{hyb} \backslash (\pi^{hyb})^{-1}((X/G)^\beth)$, then 
$\pi^{hyb}(V)$ is open in $(X/G)^{hyb}$.
<!-- end prop-39 -->
<!-- rem-17: body_md -->
By proposition 5.4 of \cite{RoyActionGroupe}, in the case where $X = \mathrm{Rat}_d$ and $G = \mathrm{SL}_2$, then $(\pi^{hyb})^{-1}((X/G)^\beth)$ is the set of rational maps with potential good reduction.
<!-- end rem-17 -->
<!-- prop-40: body_md -->
\label{Julia moves continuously on Rat_d is the same as in M_d in hybrid setting}
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ be an affine $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant subscheme of $\mathrm{Rat}_d$. Let $f \in X^{hyb}$ and let $\pi^{hyb} : X^{hyb} \subset \mathrm{Rat}_d^{hyb}\rightarrow (X/\mathrm{SL}_2)^{hyb}\subset \mathrm{M}_d^{hyb}$. Then,
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{There~is~a~flowing~neighborhood~of~}f& \in X^{hyb} \mathrm{~s.~t.~the~Julia~set~moves~continuously}\\
&\iff\\ 
\mathrm{There~is~a~flowing~neighborhood~of~} \pi^{hyb}(f)& \in (X/\mathrm{SL}_2)^{hyb} \mathrm{~s.~t.~the~Julia~set~moves~continuously.} 
\end{align*}
<!-- end prop-40 -->
<!-- rem-18: body_md -->
As in proposition \ref{Julia moves continuously on Rat_d is the same as in M_d}, here one only looks at algebraic family of rational maps, but it really is needeed since, the goal will be to study the motion of the Julia set in $\mathrm{Rat}_d^\urcorner$ and $\mathrm{M}_d^\urcorner$ and the hybrid compactification is only defined for a variety over a field $k$.
<!-- end rem-18 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
$\Longleftarrow$ It is clear.

$\implies$ Let $U$ be a flowing neighborhood of $f \in X^{hyb}$ such that the Julia set moves continuously. We may consider $W$ as in proposition \ref{Construction of SL2 invariant open in hybrid setting} which is $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant and flowing. Since the Julia set moves continuously on $W$, for each $f \in W_0$, $f$ has repelling type I points and so $f$ does not have potential good reduction and so $W \subset X^{hyb} \backslash (\pi^{hyb})^{-1}((X/G)^\beth)$. Hence, we may apply the proposition \ref{pi^hyb is open under some conditions} to show that $\pi^{hyb}(W)$ is a neighborhood of $\pi^{hyb}(f)$ and the Julia set moves continuously on $\pi^{hyb}(W)$ by definition of $W$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
\label{homeomorphism between compactifications} (Théorème 4.23, \cite{RoyActionGroupe})

Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ be an affine $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant subscheme of $\mathrm{Rat}_d$. The canonical morphism 
\begin{center}
$\omega : (X^\urcorner \backslash \lbrace f~$have potential good reduction$\rbrace \rightarrow (X/\mathrm{SL}_2)^\urcorner$
\end{center}
is a homemorphism.
<!-- end thm-9 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{continuously on compactification of Ratd is the same as on compactification of Md}
Let $\mathbb{C}$ be equipped with the hybrid norm and $X$ be an affine $\mathrm{SL}_2$-invariant subscheme of $\mathrm{Rat}_d$. Let $f\in X^\urcorner$ and $\omega : (X^\urcorner \backslash \mathcal{B})/\mathrm{SL}_2 \rightarrow (X/\mathrm{SL}_2)^\urcorner$ the homeomorphism of theorem \ref{homeomorphism between compactifications}. Then,
\begin{center}
There is a neighborhood of $f \in X^\urcorner$  such that the Julia set moves continuously
\end{center}
\begin{center}
$\iff$
\end{center}
\begin{center}
There is a neighborhood of $\omega(f) \in (X/\mathrm{SL}_2)^\urcorner$  such that the Julia set moves continuously.
\end{center}
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- defi-29: body_md -->
Let $f_i$ be a net of degenerating rational map and $z_i$ repelling points of period $l$. Then, we say that the multipliers blow-up if 
\begin{center}
$\liminf \frac{\log |(f_i^l)'(z_i)|}{\log |\mathrm{res} f_i|} >0$.
\end{center}
<!-- end defi-29 -->
<!-- rem-19: body_md -->
In the setting of hybrid spaces, the previous condition is equivalent to asking that if $\varepsilon_i \rightarrow 0$ is such that $f$ is a cluster point of $f_i^{\varepsilon_i}$ in $\mathrm{Rat}_d^{hyb}$ and $\Phi(f)$ is a cluster point of $f_i$ in $\mathrm{Rat}_d^\urcorner$, then
\begin{center}
$\liminf |(f_i^l)'(z_i)|^{\varepsilon_i} >1.$
\end{center}
It comes from the fact that since for all $a_j, b_j, |\frac{a_j^{2d}(f_i)}{\mathrm{res}(f_i)}|^{\varepsilon_i} \rightarrow |\frac{a_j^{2d}(f)}{\mathrm{res}(f)}|$. For $\max(|a_j(f_i)|,| b_j(f_i)|) = 1$, we find $\varepsilon_i \approx \frac{1}{\log|\mathrm{res} f_i|}$.
<!-- end rem-19 -->
<!-- thm-10: body_md -->
\label{InGoodHyperbolicComponentsJuliaSetContinuousIFFMulitpliersBlowUp}
Let $U$ be a hyperbolic connected component of $\mathrm{M}_d(\mathbb{C})$ such that the Julia sets do not have indifferent periodic point. Let $\tilde{f}_i$ be a degenerating net in $U$.

Then the Julia set of $\tilde{f}_i$ degenerates continuously if and only if all of the multipliers of its repelling points blow-up.
<!-- end thm-10 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
By corollary \ref{continuously on compactification of Ratd is the same as on compactification of Md} one only needs to show that the result stands for any $f_i \in \omega^{-1}(\tilde{f_i})$.

Let $f\in \delta \mathrm{Rat}_d$ be a cluster point of $f_i$. We may assume that $f_i \rightarrow f$. One needs to show that $J(f_i) \rightarrow J(f) \iff$ any multiplier of repelling point blows up.

Let $z_i$ be a repelling point of period $l$ of each $f_i$ and let $C^l$ denote the closed analytic subspace of $\mathrm{Rat}_d^{hyb} \times \mathbb{P}^{1,hyb}$ which characterizes the periodic point of period $l$. We may assume that $z_i$ are all in the same connected component of $C^l$. Let $z \in C^l\cap \mathrm{pr}^{-1}(f)$ a cluster point of the $z_i$. We may assume that $(f_i, z_i) \rightarrow (f,z)$ and so, there exists $\varepsilon_i$ such that $(f_i, z_i)^\epsilon_i \rightarrow (f,z)$ in $(\mathrm{Rat}_d \times \mathbb{P}^1)^{hyb}$.

Then $z$ is a repelling point of period $l$ if and only if $|(f^l)'(z)| = \lim |(f_i^l)'(z_i)|^{\varepsilon_i} >1$ if and only if the multipliers of the repelling points $z_i$ blow-up.

Since the $f_i$ do not have indifferent point in their Julia set, then by theorem \ref{Julia set moves continuously hybrid setting}:
\begin{align*}
J(f_i) \rightarrow J(f) &\iff \mathrm{~all~indifferent~point~of~}f\mathrm{~come~from~non~repelling~points~of~}f_i\\
&\iff \mathrm{~no~indifferent~point~of~}f\mathrm{~comes~from~repelling~points~of~}f_i\\
&\iff \mathrm{~all~multipliers~blow-up.}
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- rem-20: body_md -->
During this section, we worked with net instead of sequences because it gives a more general setting and because the hybrid spaces over $\mathbb{C}$ are not known to be angelic, nevertheless it is possible to only work with sequences and not losing any generality. To do this, instead of considering hybrid spaces as spaces over $\mathbb{C}$ with the hybrid norm, one can consider $\mathbb{Q}[i]$ equipped with its archimedean place and then equip it with a hybrid norm. Hence, theses hybrid spaces are angelic and all the results presented remain true. Instead of seing $\mathrm{Rat}_d$ as a $\mathbb{C}$ variety, one sees it as a $\mathbb{Q}[i]$ variety. The drawback of this is that $\mathrm{Rat}_{d, \mathbb{Q}[i]}^\urcorner$ does not have the same boundary as $\mathrm{Rat}_{d, \mathbb{C}}^\urcorner$. They both have $\mathrm{Rat}_d(\mathbb{C})$ as a open dense subset but the boundary of $\mathrm{Rat}_{d, \mathbb{Q}[i]}^\urcorner$ is smaller : we have a surjective projection $\delta \mathrm{Rat}_{d, \mathbb{C}}^\urcorner \rightarrow \delta \mathrm{Rat}_{d, \mathbb{Q}[i]}^\urcorner$. Hence some nets share the same limit on $\mathrm{Rat}_{d, \mathbb{Q}[i]}^\urcorner$ but not on $\mathrm{Rat}_{d, \mathbb{C}}^\urcorner$.
<!-- end rem-20 -->
